subs: Beds on its Medicare cost report. A licensed bed count usually runs higher.
Every intensive and special care unit counts: adult, cardiac, surgical, burn, neonatal and pediatric.
Each inpatient stay that ended counts once, whoever paid for it.
All inpatient days divided by discharges. Answer in days, like 4.5.
Patient days divided by the bed days it had available.
Medicare Advantage plans included. Counted in days spent in a bed, not in people.
Medicaid managed care plans included. Counted in days spent in a bed, not in people.
Two half-time employees count as one. Hospital payroll only: not clinics, not contract staff.
From AHRQ's 2023 list of who owns which hospital, matched to Medicare's hospital list.
Small rural hospitals with 25 inpatient beds at most, paid by Medicare on their costs.
By the county each hospital sits in, as CMS records it.
Every one of its hospitals' latest Medicare cost report, added up.
Biggest by beds on its cost report. The answer names the hospital.
Two half-time employees count as one. Hospital payrolls only: clinics, offices and any health plan are left out.

questions.q: How many full-time-equivalent employees did Ridgeview Medical Center have on its payroll in 2024?
questions.why: No other Ridgeview Medical Center hospital reports more; Ridgeview Sibley Medical Center is next at 79. About 10.1 for every bed.

questions.q: How many full-time-equivalent employees did Ridgeview Sibley Medical Center have on its payroll in 2024?
questions.why: That ranks second of 3 Ridgeview Medical Center hospitals; Ridgeview Medical Center has the most, 1,293. About 4.0 for every bed.

questions.q: How many full-time-equivalent employees did Minnesota Valley Health Center have on its payroll in 2024?
questions.why: That is the fewest of 3 Ridgeview Medical Center hospitals; Ridgeview Medical Center has the most, 1,293. About 5.3 for every bed.

questions.q: How many full-time-equivalent employees do Ridgeview Medical Center's hospitals have on payroll, added together?
questions.why: From all 3 hospitals' latest cost reports, mostly 2024.

questions.q: What percent of Ridgeview Medical Center's inpatient days in 2024 were for Medicare patients?
questions.why: Traditional Medicare was 32 percent and Medicare Advantage plans 25 percent.

questions.q: What percent of Ridgeview Medical Center's inpatient days in 2024 were for Medicaid patients?
questions.why: Traditional Medicaid was 6 percent and Medicaid managed care plans 7 percent.

questions.q: Across all of Ridgeview Medical Center's hospitals, what percent of inpatient days were for Medicare patients?
questions.why: Across every U.S. hospital's cost report it is 44 percent.

questions.q: Across all of Ridgeview Medical Center's hospitals, what percent of inpatient days were for Medicaid patients?
questions.why: Across every U.S. hospital's cost report it is 24 percent.

questions.q: How many beds did Ridgeview Medical Center report to Medicare for 2024?
questions.why: No other Ridgeview Medical Center hospital reports more; Ridgeview Sibley Medical Center is next at 20 beds.

questions.q: How many beds did Ridgeview Sibley Medical Center report to Medicare for 2024?
questions.why: That ranks second of 3 Ridgeview Medical Center hospitals; Ridgeview Medical Center has the most, 128 beds.

questions.q: How many beds did Minnesota Valley Health Center report to Medicare for 2024?
questions.why: That is the fewest of 3 Ridgeview Medical Center hospitals; Ridgeview Medical Center has the most, 128 beds.

questions.q: How many intensive care beds did Ridgeview Medical Center report to Medicare for 2024?
questions.why: That is 20 percent of its 128 beds.

questions.q: How many inpatient discharges did Ridgeview Medical Center report for 2024?
questions.why: About 14 a day.

questions.q: How many days did the average inpatient stay last at Ridgeview Medical Center in 2024?
questions.why: Across the cost reports of U.S. general hospitals it averages 5.0 days.

questions.q: On an average day in 2024, what percent of Ridgeview Medical Center's beds had a patient in them?
questions.why: No other Ridgeview Medical Center hospital ran fuller; Minnesota Valley Health Center is next at 18 percent.

questions.q: On an average day in 2024, what percent of Ridgeview Sibley Medical Center's beds had a patient in them?
questions.why: That is the emptiest of 3 Ridgeview Medical Center hospitals; Ridgeview Medical Center ran fullest, 53 percent.

questions.q: On an average day in 2024, what percent of Minnesota Valley Health Center's beds had a patient in them?
questions.why: That ranks second of 3 Ridgeview Medical Center hospitals; Ridgeview Medical Center ran fullest, 53 percent.

questions.q: How many hospitals does Ridgeview Medical Center run, by the federal list of health systems?
questions.why: All of them are in Minnesota. A system's own count can differ: it may count campuses on their own, or hospitals that joined after 2023.

questions.q: How many of Ridgeview Medical Center's hospitals are critical access hospitals?
questions.why: They are Minnesota Valley Health Center and Ridgeview Sibley Medical Center.

questions.q: How many of Ridgeview Medical Center's hospitals are outside a metropolitan area?
questions.why: They are Ridgeview Sibley Medical Center.

questions.q: How many beds do Ridgeview Medical Center's hospitals report to Medicare, added together?
questions.why: From all 3 hospitals' latest cost reports, mostly 2024.

questions.q: How many beds does Ridgeview Medical Center's biggest hospital report to Medicare?
questions.why: It is Ridgeview Medical Center. Ridgeview Sibley Medical Center is next, with 20.

questions.q: How many intensive care beds do Ridgeview Medical Center's hospitals report to Medicare, added together?
questions.why: That is 16 percent of their 157 beds. From all 3 hospitals' latest cost reports, mostly 2024.

questions.q: How many inpatient discharges did Ridgeview Medical Center's hospitals report in a year, added together?
questions.why: About 14 a day. From all 3 hospitals' latest cost reports, mostly 2024.
